You use time clauses to give information about time and sequence in future actions.
You use the words once, while, as soon as, until, If, When, Before and After in time clauses.
Future time clauses explain what needs to happen or which condition needs to be satisfied before a future event can occur.
You use the first conditional with these time clauses.
<ul>As soon as/Until/If/When/Before/After + Subject + Simple Present tense, Subject + will/be going to + Simple Present tense
Once means at the same time. An action in the future will occur the moment the action introduced by the time clause finishes.

Example:
    Once I finish the next session, I'm going to move to a small studio space.

While means during the duration of a future action. The action introduced by the time clause will still be going on when another future action starts. You normally use while after the main clause.
Example:
    I'll meditate while you finish your project.
If means on the condition that ...
When means at the time of doing something.
Once I finish the next session of coaching, I am going to be moving to a small studio space.
As soon as my classes are done, I'll definitely come and meditate.
Before he does the talk, I am going to meet up and have lunch with him. I think you should come.
When I finish my course, I'll call him and make arrangements.
Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tenses

You use the Future Continuous to talk about something that will be in progress in the future.
You use the Future Perfect to talk about something that will be finished by a certain time in the future.
The action will have started before that moment but it will not have finished at that moment.
I will be working at 4 p.m. tomorrow.
The person will start work at some point in the future and be working at 4 p.m. It is not clear when the person will stop working.
There are two ways to use the Future Continuous tense:
• You use the Future Continuous to indicate that a longer action in the future will be interrupted by a shorter action in the future.
Structure:</br><ul> will + be + present participle of the verb

Example:
    I'll be starting my own mindfulness meditation course soon.
• You use the Future Continuous to express the idea that two actions will be happening at the same time. The actions are parallel. You use two Future Continuous actions in the same sentence.
Structure: </br><ul> am/is/are + going to be + present participle

Example:
    I am going to be starting a great project soon so I'm going to be living near the studio for a while.
When you use the Future Perfect, you can sometimes think of the Future Perfect tense like the Present Perfect tense, but instead of your viewpoint being in the present, it is in the future.

The Future Perfect has two forms:
    will have + past participle, or
      am/is/are + going to have + past participle

Example:
    He'll have returned to Italy by the end of the month.

images.text:
Vanessa: It's great to see you! How's the life-coaching going?
Amy: It's been too long since we've seen each other. I'll be starting my own mindfulness meditation course soon. Once I finish the next session of coaching, I am going to be moving to a small studio space.

Vanessa: As soon as my classes are done, I'll definitely come and meditate. Your life-coaching helped me discover my vocation. It was one of the best investments I've made. Will you be doing the mindfulness every day?
Amy: Yes. I'll have moved out of my house, so I will be living and working at the studio. What about you? What projects will you be starting next season?

Vanessa : I'll have completed my courses by then. I hope I'll have made connections with investors too. I'm so stoked! Until I finish my courses, I am not going to talk about this with too many people so can you keep it under wraps?
Amy: My lips are sealed. When you are ready, I will be here for you, and I happen to have a relative in the gourmet business. He owned Le Papillon Bleu and is a serious investor now. He's in Italy, but he'll have returned by the end of the month.

Vanessa: You mean Emile Beaulieu? Wow! He will be investing in our restaurant Management Program. Apparently, when he's back from Italy he'll be giving a talk at our college.
Amy: You're kidding! Before he does the talk, I am going to meet up and have lunch with him. I think you should come. When I finish my course, I'll call him and make arrangements.

Vanessa: I hope I'll have calmed down by then.
Amy: We will meditate beforehand to keep your nerves at bay. You are optimistic, non-judgemental and you have impeccable taste in. Emile will love you!
